## Making What Matters: Jerry Horning


Innovation is at the heart of how Graco helps customers work more efficiently, solve challenges and achieve results. Behind many of those innovations are employees whose ideas have shaped the products customers rely on every day.


One of those innovators is Jerry Horning, principal mechanical engineer in Graco’s Contractor Division. During more than 27 years with the company, Horning has been a named inventor on close to 300 utility and design patents worldwide and has contributed to several product advancements. His work has helped transform product lines and improve performance.


#### A passion for creating from an early age


Horning’s drive to build and innovate began long before his career at Graco.


He recalls an elementary school project in which students were asked to create a model spaceship to hang from the classroom ceiling. While many students completed the assignment, Horning took it a step further by adding a spacewalker alongside his spacecraft.


That was not the last time that Horning pushed beyond expectations. Later in junior high, Horning added retractable sheet-metal wings to a welded bug project, earning an A and some lighthearted teasing from classmates for “raising the bar.” Years later in college, Horning designed and fabricated a custom assembly tool and part-feeding system for a robotics competition, dramatically improving assembly speed and demonstrating the same problem-solving mindset that would later define his engineering career. Looking back, Horning sees a common thread throughout those experiences: a desire to figure out how things work and find better ways to make them work better.


That curiosity and persistence stemmed from the time spent with his grandfathers. One operated a farm and could fix just about anything, with bailing wire and pliers readily available, as well as a work shed filled with tools and mason jars full of fasteners, hardware and miscellaneous parts. Horning was fascinated by the possibilities those materials represented.


His other grandfather was a pattern maker with a workshop filled with woodworking and metal fabrication equipment. Among the many projects seen in the workshop, Horning’s grandfather also taught him how to use a mill and lathe as Horning developed a custom tool design for a robotics class. More importantly, he took the time to teach Horning how things worked rather than doing the work for him.


Those experiences created an early interest in building and problem-solving that followed Horning into adulthood, from his own workshop to the engineering projects he works on at Graco.


#### A breakthrough innovation: The portable airless sprayer


Among Horning’s many contributions, one stands out for its impact on Graco’s Contractor business: the portable airless sprayer.


The product helped reshape multiple product lines and demonstrated how innovative thinking can create entirely new possibilities for customers.


Horning still remembers being assigned to the project. At the time, Dave Thompson, now president of Graco’s Contractor Division, had a vision for a handheld airless sprayer but needed help in bringing the concept to life.


Thompson challenged Horning to turn the idea into a working product.


After extensive design and development work, Horning helped create the first functional handheld prototype. He later demonstrated it to Pat McHale, who was Graco’s CEO at the time.


“I was very fortunate that Dave Thompson gave me the assignment to design, develop and demonstrate the first functional handheld product,” Horning said. “I was given an opportunity that could have gone to anyone. I’m grateful I had the chance to help bring the idea to life.”


The success of the portable airless sprayer became one of many examples of how collaboration, technical expertise and persistence can translate ideas into products customers depend on.


#### Solving challenges through engineering


Another achievement Horning considers among his most significant came from a simple but important question: How can we make a pump rod last longer?


Many Graco pumps operate in demanding environments where durability is critical. To improve wear resistance and product longevity, Horning worked with his team to develop a specialized ceramic rod.


The project required rounds of testing, evaluation of different materials and multiple design iterations. The result was a more durable solution that provided both performance advantages for the customers and competitive advantages for Graco through cost savings and product differentiation.


Like many breakthroughs, the innovation was built on persistence, willingness to experiment and a commitment to solving real-world challenges.


#### Turning ideas into real-world solutions


When asked what advice he would give aspiring engineers, Horning emphasizes the importance of hands-on experience.


“In order to be a good engineer, designer, or whatever it may be, it is important to get hands-on experience,” Horning said. “It’s one thing to create your idea on paper as a theory. It’s another to understand how that idea will translate in the real world.”


Horning said it is important to try new things, even when failure is a possibility, because every experience offers an opportunity to learn. He also stressed the importance of persistence and viewing challenges as opportunities instead of road blocks.


That mindset has guided Horning throughout his career, helping him bridge the gap between concepts and practical solutions.


#### A legacy that lasts


While patents and recognition are meaningful milestones, Horning believes that there are other ways to measure success.


"What I’m really proud of is my legacy of designs that are used in various Graco products,” Horning said. “It is very rewarding to see things I designed and collaborated on with co-workers become part of so many Graco products.”


For Horning, seeing designs created decades ago continue to serve customers today is one of the most rewarding aspects of his career.


He also credits Graco for fostering an environment where innovation can thrive. Through collaboration, support and the freedom to explore new ideas, Horning has been able to turn concepts into products that continue to make an impact.


Horning’s story reflects the ingenuity, dedication and customer-focused innovation that helps Graco continue moving materials that matter.
